plain: having a special right or protection others lack

webster.text: Invested with a privilege; enjoying a peculiar right or immunity.

example.quote: They shall in all cases, except treason, felony and breach of the peace, be privileged from arrest during their attendance at the session of their respective houses, and in going to and returning from the same; and for any speech or debate in either house, they shall not be questioned in any other place.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 12, 1787
